newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil says renews product, oil ship charters.
newsitem.headline: Statoil says renews product, oil ship charters.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday it had renewed charters for product carriers Capella and Zoja II and the shuttle tanker Stena Savonita.

The two 29,000-tonne product carriers will stay in the group's fleet for another year, while the shuttle tanker has been rehired for 22 months after the present charter expires on July 1, Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said.
Built in 1995, Capella is owned by Prisco Maritime Ltd and managed by Milbros Shipping in Oslo. Latvian Shipping Co owns the 1989-built Zoja II, which is managed by Latmar Columbian Ltd of Cyprus.
Statoil said both vessels will continue to sail in northern Europe, mainly carrying refined products.
Stens Savonita can load 730,000 barrels of crude and will work in the British sector of the North Sea. It was built in 1992 and converted to a shuttle tanker two years later.

It is owned by Nordic American Shipping in Sandefjord near Oslo and has been chartered to Statoil since late last year for field tests on the UK Claire development west of Shetland and Banff in the British North Sea.
